test.name: An indirect record's date window is sized to the record creator's lifespan, not the subject's own window
test.description: caroline-probate-creator-lifespan: q_001 asks which probate/estate record names Caroline Voss's father, for a subject born 1839 with no other dated fact besides a circa-1858 marriage. A sound plan sizes the probate item's date_range to the FATHER's plausible lifespan (roughly Caroline's birth year through birth+60, i.e. up to circa 1899) rather than to Caroline's own early-life research window. Guards the SKILL.md 'size an indirect record's date window to its likely CREATOR' Key selection principle (issue #1472, Rule 2), reproduced against this fixture per the issue's own instruction to verify the craft point before treating it as settled.

input.user_message: Create the first research plan for q_001 — which probate or estate record names Caroline Voss's father?

judge_context: The plan MUST include at least one probate/estate plan item targeting Caroline's father. Its `date_range` must extend to approximately the father's plausible lifespan — roughly Caroline's birth year (1839) through birth+55 to birth+65 (circa 1894-1904) — not stop at or shortly after Caroline's own circa-1858 marriage or any other subject-centric bound well short of that.
How the probate item's date_range is sized is what Record type selection turns on for this test. Assess whose plausible lifespan bounds the window: the record's creator, or the research subject.
The item's rationale should say whose lifespan set the window's bounds (the father's, not Caroline's) — ideal but grade generously if the reasoning is present even without using that exact phrase.
Additional breadth items (marriage records for Caroline's own parents, land records, cemetery records) strengthen the plan but are not individually required.
